FlyRockPlatTiles.name: Draw staggered 8x8 platform (rock, orange)
summary: Graphics for the rock and orange platforms (sprites $56, $58, $5D, $5E), reached from CODE_01B2D1; starts with the rock tile table.
Draws 5 tiles (9 for sprite $5E): even slots form a top row, odd slots a row 16 pixels lower, each tile 8 pixels right of the last.
Tiles come from DiagPlatTiles (sprite >= $5B) or the rock table; all but the first two are X-flipped.
Quirk: the short rock platform path (sprite < $5B, $00 = 0) is unused; the short orange one gets its end caps patched in.

InvisBlkMainRt.name: Make Mario stand on or bump sprite
summary: Long-callable wrapper (sets data bank) used by sprites in bank 3. Makes the sprite a solid block for Mario.
CODE_01B457 does the work: standing on top snaps Mario to the sprite and carries him by [$1528]; touching from below bumps
him down (sprites >= $83 also start a hit animation); touching the side pushes him out via CODE_01B505.
Returns: carry set if Mario is standing on the sprite. Sets [$1471] = 1 when standing.

s01B4F9.name: Table: Mario X offsets for side push

s01B505.name: Push Mario out sideways
summary: Places Mario beside the sprite: X = sprite X + offset, picked by which side he is on (SubHorizPos) and sprite type
($A9 uses the second pair, $9C/$BB/$60/$49 the third), and zeroes his X speed. Returns carry clear.

OrangePlatform.name: Orange platform main routine
summary: Sprite $5E. Normal state runs Platforms2. The rest (state non-zero) is unreferenced: draw, move on X and run away to the right
(X speed 8) once Mario touches it.

FloatingSpikeBall.name: Floating spike ball main routine
summary: Sprite $A4. Runs Platforms2 while sprite status is 8 (normal); otherwise only draws.

Platforms2.name: Floating platforms and spike ball physics
summary: Shared main routine for sprites $5B-$5D (floating/falling platforms) and $A4 (floating spike ball). Applies gravity, water
buoyancy, sinking under Mario's weight and a dip when he jumps off, damps Y speed, then despawns and draws.
Platforms use the solid interaction (CODE_01B457); the spike ball hurts Mario instead.
Uses [$185E] = Mario on platform now, [$151C] = same flag last frame, [$164A] = sprite in water.

FloatMineGfxProp.name: Draw floating spike ball
summary: Table of tile properties followed by the graphics routine for sprite $A4: four 16x16 tiles in a 2x2 block around the sprite,
tile $AA or $AC alternating every 16 frames, with X/Y flips from the table.

TurnBlockBridge.name: Turn block bridge, horizontal and vertical
summary: Sprite $59. [$151C] is how far the outer blocks are from the center (0-$20). State bit 0 selects extending or retracting, and the
state increments at each end after a $40 frame pause, so bit 1 flips every second step and the bridge alternates between axes.

HorzTurnBlkBridge.name: Turn block bridge, horizontal only
summary: Sprite $5A. Same as TurnBlockBridge but the state toggles between 0 and 1, so it only moves along X.
CODE_01B710 (included here) draws five turn blocks (tile $40): the center plus two on each side at full and half extension,
with the axis chosen by state bit 1.

FinishOAMWrite.name: Finish OAM write (long wrapper)
summary: Sets the data bank to $01 and calls FinishOAMWriteRt, which sets the OAM size bits and hides offscreen tiles.
Parameters: Y = tile size, A = number of tiles - 1.
